description: Make transaction categorization learn from household history so parents stop re-categorizing the same merchants every month. When a parent categorizes a transaction, Family Pulse remembers the merchant-fingerprint-to-category association and applies it automatically on future syncs. High-confidence matches auto-apply silently with provenance; lower-confidence matches surface as one-tap suggestions instead of blank uncategorized rows. Fully deterministic in v1 — no LLM calls.

timing.gatingCondition: None. Builds on existing merchant-normalizer fingerprints (Feature 19) and the categorization pipeline (Feature 1/4). Independent of Feature 23 push notifications.

principles: The parent's manual categorization is the training signal; the system learns silently from normal use with zero extra dialogs
Explicit category_rules always outrank learned associations; learned associations outrank Plaid taxonomy fallback
A manually-set category is never overwritten by any automatic pass — manual is terminal
Auto-apply only on unanimous history (every prior occurrence of this fingerprint has the same category, minimum occurrence count met); anything less is a suggestion, not an action
Suggestions are one-tap accept/reject and must work well on mobile — the goal is turning categorization from typing into confirming
A rejected suggestion is remembered and never re-offered for the same fingerprint-category pair

Contextual categories don't teach: categories flagged exclude_from_learning (e.g. Vacation, where dining/gas/flights all get stamped regardless of merchant) never create learned rules, never count in history votes, and are never suggested — mirroring the existing exclude_from_baseline pattern from migration 016
Every automatically assigned category carries visible provenance (rule / learned / plaid) so trust is inspectable
V1 is pure SQL + deterministic code — no OpenAI calls anywhere in this feature
SECRETS INVARIANT: learned rules store only merchant fingerprints and category ids — no tokens, no account identifiers beyond existing transaction rows

techStack.testing: node:test for learning/vote/precedence logic with fixture histories; Playwright for suggestion accept/reject flows on the transactions page

userStories.title: Manual categorization silently teaches the system
acceptanceCriteria: When a parent sets or changes a transaction's category via PUT /api/transactions/:id/category, Family Pulse upserts a learned_category_rules row keyed by the transaction's merchant fingerprint (buildMerchantFingerprint) with the chosen category
The bulk categorize endpoint records the same learning for every affected transaction's fingerprint
Re-categorizing a merchant to a different category updates the learned association to the new category rather than accumulating conflicting rows
Learning capture never blocks or fails the categorization request — learning errors are logged and swallowed
Transactions with an 'unknown' fingerprint (no usable merchant text) do not create learned rules

Categorizing into a category flagged exclude_from_learning creates and updates no learned rule — the vacation-stamping workflow (Mobil charge stamped Vacation) must leave the merchant's everyday learned association untouched
Kid role cannot trigger learning because kids cannot categorize (existing guard remains intact)
userStories.testStrategy: node:test covering upsert-on-change semantics, unknown-fingerprint skip, and non-blocking failure behavior via the existing categories/transactions API test harness.

userStories.title: History vote auto-applies categories on sync
acceptanceCriteria: During the post-sync categorization pass, each uncategorized non-transfer non-hidden transaction is fingerprinted and checked against learned_category_rules and against historical categorized transactions sharing the fingerprint

If a learned rule exists (applies immediately at count 1 — operator categorization is trusted), or if all prior categorized occurrences of the fingerprint (minimum 3) agree on one category, the category is auto-applied with categorization_source = 'learned'

Precedence is explicit category_rules first, then learned associations; Plaid taxonomy no longer silently auto-applies — it becomes suggestion-only (behavior change from Feature 1 documented in the migration notes)
Transactions whose category was set manually (categorization_source = 'manual') are never touched by any automatic pass, including applyRulesRetroactive

History votes exclude priors whose current category is flagged exclude_from_learning from both numerator and denominator — vacation-stamped occurrences of a merchant neither vote for Vacation nor break unanimity for the merchant's everyday category
The sync log line reports counts by source: rules, learned, plaid, suggested
categorizeMany avoids per-row queries for the history vote — fingerprint histories are computed in bulk (single grouped query), keeping sync time flat as transaction count grows
userStories.testStrategy: node:test with fixture histories: unanimous ≥3 auto-applies, 2-occurrence unanimity does not, explicit rule beats conflicting learned rule, manual rows untouched, bulk-query behavior asserted via result counts.

userStories.title: Low-confidence matches become one-tap suggestions
acceptanceCriteria: When history for a fingerprint is majority-but-not-unanimous, or the only signal is the Plaid taxonomy mapping for a never-seen merchant, the transaction gets suggested_category_id and suggestion_source populated instead of a silent category assignment
Categories flagged exclude_from_learning are never proposed as suggestions
The transactions page shows uncategorized rows with a suggestion as a compact chip: suggested category name with accept and reject affordances, usable one-handed on mobile
Accepting applies the category, marks categorization_source = 'manual' semantics for learning purposes (it reinforces the learned rule), and clears the suggestion fields
Rejecting clears the suggestion and records the fingerprint-category rejection so the same pair is never suggested again; a different category may still be suggested later
An 'Uncategorized with suggestions' count is visible from the transactions page filter area so the review pass is discoverable
Suggestion accept/reject endpoints are parent-only
userStories.testStrategy: node:test for suggestion generation thresholds, rejection memory, and auth guards; Playwright for chip rendering, accept updating the row in place, and reject removing the chip.

userStories.title: Provenance is visible and manual always wins
acceptanceCriteria: Transaction API payloads include categorization_source (manual, rule, learned, plaid, or null)
The transaction detail overlay shows a small provenance badge explaining why the current category was applied
Manually changing a category on an auto-categorized transaction sets categorization_source = 'manual' and updates the learned association per LAC-024-001
Existing transactions are backfilled to categorization_source = 'manual' where a category is set, so history is protected from retroactive automatic passes from day one
applyRulesRetroactive respects the manual guard and reports how many rows it skipped for that reason
userStories.testStrategy: node:test for source transitions and retroactive-pass guard; Playwright spot-check for badge presence in the detail overlay.

userStories.title: Learned rules are inspectable for debugging
acceptanceCriteria: A parent-only GET endpoint lists learned rules with fingerprint, category, occurrence count, last-applied timestamp, and rejection pairs
The endpoint is read-only in v1 — no learned-rule editing UI (deleting a bad association happens by re-categorizing a transaction, which updates it)

Learned rule and rejection tables are included in db/clear-linked-data.js preservation notes with an explicit decision on clear-vs-preserve (preserve, since they encode household intent like categories and category_rules)
userStories.testStrategy: node:test for endpoint shape and parent-only guard.

medium: A single early miscategorization could propagate silently via auto-apply. Mitigation: unanimous-history threshold of 3, provenance badge, manual correction immediately rewrites the learned rule, and the review-queue path for anything ambiguous.

Fingerprint collisions (two genuinely different merchants normalizing to the same fingerprint) could cross-categorize. Mitigation: fingerprints already drive recurring detection reliably for this household; collisions surface visibly via provenance and are correctable in one tap.
low: History-vote query cost on large transaction tables. Mitigation: single grouped query per sync pass plus index on the new fingerprint-backed lookup.
Suggestion chips could clutter the transactions list. Mitigation: chips render only on uncategorized rows with a pending suggestion.

Backfilling categorization_source = 'manual' for all existing categorized rows slightly overstates manual intent for rows that were originally rule/plaid-applied. Accepted: it errs on the side of never clobbering existing data.
operational: If the deferred LLM fallback ships later, it must feed the suggestion queue only — never auto-apply — preserving the deterministic-auto-apply invariant.
Learned rules encode household intent; back them up with the same cadence as categories and category_rules.
